text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- Paavo Lipponen's five-party government is taking a breather after past tough decisions and ahead of next autumn's tough incomes settlement talks and the historic EMU decision.
- Interest in bond investment is rising: low yields do not offer big returns but investors are increasingly cautious.
- Russians may oppose plans to build an oil pipeline from Russia to Porvoo, seeking more control of transport of oil exports which increasingly go via foreign ports.
- Tourism lobby expects travel through Finland to other countries to rise substantially in coming years.
- PM Lipponen has moved to live with his girlfriend Paivi Hertzberg in her house in suburban Jollas, but continues to keep his official residence for practical reasons.
KAUPPALEHTI
- EU countries' income tax rates vary widely and differences have not diminished in the past year, British study shows.
- Increasing gateway traffic could bring Finland some two billion markka in revenue; national carrier Finnair's gateway income is already almost a billion markka.
AAMULEHTI
- Contagious diseases are today a bigger global threat than ever before, Professor Pauli Leinikki at the centre for national health says.
- Employment offices are planning to gather new information about the unemployed to improve services to potential employers.
- Ozone layer above Finland is thicker this spring than recently, and being in the sun is less harmful.
TURUN SANOMAT

- Kesko's plans to sell parts of Tuko may fail unless the European Commission approves arrangements by end April. Kesko board member Matti Halmesmaki says agreements expire then, and no extra time has been negotiated.
DEMARI
- Government will not reduce tax breaks on pension insurance saving, says PM Paavo Lipponen.
- Erkki Tuomioja, leader of the Social Democratic Party's MPs -- the largest group in parliament -- says MPs should be allowed to vote independently on EMU when the issue comes to parliament.
HUFVUDSTADSBLADET
- Pope John Paul II, meeting United Nations human rights envoy and Finland's ex-defence minister Elisabeth Rehn, thought she was American.
- Swedish People's Party's new party programme draft is a step towards the right, professor Goran Djupsund says.
